title: Implications for Singapore of G7 Agreement on Global Minimum Corporate Tax Rate
what_it_is: Implications for Singapore of G7 Agreement on Global Minimum Corporate Tax Rate

sections.label: G7 global minimum corporate tax questions
sections.summary: MPs asked the Minister for Finance about the G7 global minimum corporate tax's impact on Singapore, its revenue, tech hub status, MNCs and tax incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) how will Singapore be impacted by the landmark agreement amongst G7 nations to reform the global tax system and impose a minimum global corporate tax rate of 15%; and (b) what are the plans to mitigate adverse impact to Singapore's corporate income tax revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) what are the implications of the G7 agreement on a global minimum corporate tax for Singapore; (b) whether Singapore’s status as a tech hub will be affected; and (c) how will the tax affect multinational corporations that currently operate in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) what is the number of MNCs that currently pay less than the global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% proposed by G7; and (b) given that MNCs receive tax incentives for undertaking activities that benefit Singapore in the long run such as developing new sectors or building capabilities, whether such special tax schemes will be permissible under the proposed changes; and (c) what other levers must the Government strengthen.

sections.label: Pillar One and Pillar Two thresholds
sections.summary: The proposal sets Pillar One for MNE groups above 20 billion euros revenue and 10% profitability, and a minimum effective tax rate of at least 15% above 750 million euros.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The current proposal is that Pillar One will apply to MNE groups with global revenues above 20 billion euros and profitability above 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The G7 and IF have proposed a minimum effective tax rate of at least 15% for MNE groups with global revenues above 750 million euros.

sections.label: MNE groups meeting revenue threshold
sections.summary: Pillar Two's minimum effective tax rate applies to MNEs meeting a 750 million euro revenue threshold, with about 1,800 such MNE groups in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The current proposal, under Pillar Two, is to apply this minimum effective tax rate to MNEs that meet a certain revenue threshold, currently set at 750 million euros, as I highlighted just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are about 1,800 such MNE groups in Singapore that would meet this revenue criterion.

sections.label: Regulatory environment and capabilities support
sections.summary: Singapore will provide a conducive regulatory environment, ecosystem and infrastructure, and work with industry to build capabilities and skills for structural trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In short, we will continue to provide a conducive regulatory environment for businesses, especially for new and innovative activities, as well as a good ecosystem and infrastructure for such activities to scale up across the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also work closely with the industry to build up capabilities and skills that will enable us to stay relevant in the face of key structural trends like digitalisation and sustainability that are transforming the financial landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The key is for us to stay agile and nimble, and respond innovatively to the key global trends affecting our economy.

sections.label: Sovereign tax rights and corporate tax adjustment
sections.summary: Singapore will protect its sovereign rights on taxes and adjust its corporate tax system in line with international standards, consulting businesses and keeping compliance burden low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Number one, we will protect our sovereign rights on taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And we will make sure we adjust our corporate tax system accordingly, in line with the international standards and in close consultation with businesses in Singapore, ensuring that as far as possible, we keep a low compliance burden on businesses.

sections.label: Difficulty attracting investments as small city-state
sections.summary: With these tax changes, it will be harder for Singapore, a small city-state with no natural resources and limited land, to attract investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It has always been so and we will continue to work hard on this front.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think we should also be mindful and clear that with these tax changes, going forward, as a small city-state with no natural resources, with limited land, it will be that much harder for Singapore to attract investments.

sections.label: G7 minimum corporate tax rate
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the Minister sees the 15% effective tax rate as a number Singapore can agree to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I understand that the G7 countries had initially sought a minimum corporate tax rate of 21%, but have since agreed to lower it to 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I would like ask the Minister whether he sees this 15% effective tax rate as a number that Singapore can agree to.

sections.label: Inclusive Forum consensus on tax
sections.summary: The passage notes 130 jurisdictions including Singapore reached consensus on key parameters, including a 15% global effective minimum tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, whether the 15% tax effective rate would be enough offset for them in the short term?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And recently, 130 jurisdictions in the Inclusive Forum, including Singapore, have reached a consensus on the key parameters of the corporate tax changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That includes the global effective minimum tax rate of 15%.

sections.label: Pillar One negative impact
sections.summary: The passage states Pillar One will have a negative impact because it reallocates tax revenues from large firms to market locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the second question on Pillar One, yes, there will be a negative impact, because Pillar One means reallocating tax revenues for some of these large firms to where the markets are located.

sections.label: Tax changes harder to attract investments
sections.summary: The passage states the tax changes will make it harder for Singapore to attract investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The upshot of these tax changes, as I said just now, is that it will make it harder for Singapore to attract investments; there should be no doubt.

sections.label: MNCs larger tax burden, Singapore response
sections.summary: The passage states large MNCs will bear a larger tax burden, so Singapore must work harder on workforce, infrastructure, connectivity and business environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Basically, in a post-Pillar One and post-Pillar Two world, the large MNCs of the world will bear a larger tax burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Assuming Pillars One and Two are applied evenly, uniformly, around the world, they will have to bear a larger tax burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we, on our part, will therefore have to work that much harder, whether it is on upgrading of our workforce, our infrastructure, our connectivity, our overall business environment; all of these factors will, therefore, become more salient in our ability to attract and retain investments and, ultimately, with the objective of creating good jobs for Singaporeans.
